title: Contributor Impact & Tooling Blueprint — First 100 Days
author: Asha Venkataraman
body:
Overview

Purpose: This blueprint helps new contributors (engineers, product managers, designers, and others) move from first-day orientation to sustained impact within the first 100 days at Redwood. It consolidates role-level expectations, a time-phased onboarding plan, tooling and access guidance, and the key checkpoints for early career growth. The audience is new hires, their hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

How to use this doc
- New hires: follow the first-7/30/60/100 day checklists and use the tooling quickstart table.
- Managers: run the 1:1 cadence and use the evaluation checkpoints to support leveling conversations.
- People-ops and IT: reference the provisioning SLAs and escalation contacts.

High-level goals (measurable):
- Account & dev environment fully provisioned within 48 hours (target SLA: 95%).
- First PR merged to a production-similar repo within 30 days for ICs on engineering teams.
- Role-level impact demonstration (owner of a small cross-functional task) within 60–100 days.

1) Time-phased onboarding blueprint

Day 0–7: Foundation (orientation + access)
- Complete new-hire orientation and legal forms.
- Receive laptop, Slack, SSO + SAML access, and Redwood internal accounts.
- Goals: Meet manager, buddy assignment, complete security training, join primary team channel.
- Deliverable: ``Intro note`` posted in team channel summarizing background and initial focus.

Day 8–30: Practical ramp (access + small wins)
- Complete guided walkthroughs of the codebase / product areas relevant to role.
- Complete first small onboarding task: bug fix, doc update, or feature spike.
- Attend product and architecture overview sessions.
- Deliverable: PR merged and a short write-up of the learning and next steps.

Day 31–60: Contribution & ownership
- Lead a small cross-functional task (PM, Designer, Eng) with clear acceptance criteria.
- Begin regular 1:1s and growth conversations.
- Start a personal learning plan tied to role competencies.
- Deliverable: Role-specific milestone (e.g., customer bug triage ownership, A/B test instrumented).

Day 61–100: Scale impact & career alignment
- Run a retrospective on the first 90 days with manager and adjust growth plan.
- Present a short demo of your contribution to the team.
- Prepare for the 100-day checkpoint: evidence of impact mapped to competency rubric.
- Deliverable: 100-day impact memo (one-page) and suggested next objectives.

2) Role clarity and contribution rubric (how we measure early impact)

We use a concise rubric to set expectations across contributors. Each rubric element maps to behaviors managers and hires can observe during the first 100 days.
- Ownership: takes responsibility for a discrete work item end-to-end (design, implementation, rollout).
- Collaboration: communicates clearly, solicits feedback, and coordinates cross-functional tasks.
- Quality: produces code/doc/designs that meet our standards and testing expectations.
- Speed & judgement: balances speed to delivery with appropriate risk controls.
- Learning: demonstrates role-specific upskilling and uses feedback.

Example success signals by day 60:
- At least one merged PR touching production-like systems (engineering).
- Documented customer/feature context and suggested next steps (product/design).
- Ownership of a recurring on-call rotation shadow or incident postmortem contribution (SRE adjacent roles).

3) Career ladder primer and early leveling conversations

This document does not replace the full career ladder guides. Use it to anchor early leveling dialogs:
- Entry IC (L1–L2): focus on execution, learning systems, and asking questions.
- Mid IC (L3–L4): deliver independent features, mentor peers, and contribute to design.
- Senior IC (L5+): lead cross-team initiatives, influence architecture, coach others.

Manager checklist for first 100 days:
1. Set clear 30/60/100-day success criteria the first week.
2. Schedule weekly 1:1s and a 100-day review.
3. Assign a buddy and at least one small initial project.
4. Review tooling/access status at 48 hours and escalate if incomplete.
5. Document evidence and provide formative feedback at day 30 and day 60.

4) Benefits & perks snapshot (quick reference)

High level (link to full benefits pages in People Ops):
- Health: medical, dental, vision with flexible pre-tax options.
- Leave: 20 days PTO baseline, parental leave policy, caregiver leave.
- Stipends: home office, commuter, learning & conference budget.
- Wellness: counseling and resilience programs, monthly wellbeing sessions.

Perk highlights relevant to early contributors:
- Learning credit: $1500/year for books, courses, and conferences — use for early skill acceleration.
- Hardware refresh cadence: 36 months, expedited requests considered for role needs.

5) Internal tools quickstart (provisioning & common commands)

Provisioning SLAs:
- Accounts provisioned: target 48 hours for 95% of hires.
- Dev environment (local with dockerized stacks): target 5 business days for full reproduction if a remote environment is required.

Required first-access checklist (owner: IT/PeopleOps):
- SSO/SAML, Slack, Gmail/Workspace, Okta, HR portal, ExpenseTool, Internal wiki access, GitHub org access.

Common commands & examples (engineering)
- Request GH org membership (CLI):
  redwood-tools request-access --team=eng --repo=core --reason="onboarding-PR"
- Start a reproducible local dev stack:
  ./dev/launch.sh --profile=small
- Check internal API key usage:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDBOX_TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood/v1/keys

Tooling access table (quick map)
| Purpose | Tool | Who to contact |
|---|---|---|
| Chat & async comms | Slack | it-support@redwood.com |
| Code hosting | GitHub (org) | eng-platform@redwood.com |
| CI/CD | Buildkite / Argo | infra-sre@redwood.com |
| Docs & wiki | Confluence | docs-team@redwood.com |
| Expense & hardware requests | SpendPortal | finance-ops@redwood.com |

6) Communication norms & working model

Hybrid-first philosophy: Redwood supports a distributed workforce. Teams should set shared norms for which days are core overlap, meeting windows, and calendar etiquette.
- Core hours recommendation: 10:00–16:00 local for team collaboration.
- Async-first expectation: document decisions, use PR descriptions, and summarize meetings in Confluence notes.

Meeting & calendar guidance:
- Default meeting length: 25/50 mins to create focus buffers.
- Decision ownership: every recurring decision should have an owner and a timestamped note logged in Confluence.

7) 100-day checkpoint and promotion readiness signals

The 100-day checkpoint is a formative review, not a promotion review. It is used to:
- Align on demonstrated competencies against the ladder.
- Agree on the next 6-month objectives.
- Decide on any accelerated development actions (mentoring, shadowing, targeted projects).

Promotion readiness signals (early indicators):
- Regular independent delivery and fewer rework cycles.
- Clear examples of mentorship and cross-team collaboration.
- Ownership of a measurable product outcome.

8) Escalation and support contacts

If provisioning or tooling is delayed beyond SLAs: escalate to people-ops@redwood.com and copy your manager.
Security or access incidents: security@redwood.com (24/7 pager for on-call incidents).
Hardware or expense disputes: finance-ops@redwood.com.

Appendices
A. 100-day impact memo template (one paragraph each): Context, action taken, outcome, follow-ups.
B. Link map: onboarding-toolchain, competency maps, full benefits site, code of conduct, security awareness guide.

Owner and maintenance
- Document owner: People Ops (Asha Venkataraman).
- Review cadence: annual with immediate updates for tool or policy changes.
- Last reviewed: 2026-09-15.
